identification: Five framed works. (1)-(2) Two Bea Maddock 'Red Text' sheets, Roman numerals XXV and XXVI lower right, Genesis 10-11 text (Table of Nations, Tower of Babel) etched from zinc plates, red-brown ink on handmade NZ flax paper coated with wax, simple timber frames; typed statement on the back says the forty framed works called RED TEXT were etched at Ritchies Mill studio, Launceston in 1984 (shown in 'In the interim and red text', Snake Pit Gallery Launceston, July 1994). (3) Pen-style figure of a man from behind holding umbrella and bag: on close look the line is stitched thread (free-motion machine embroidery) on fabric, not pen; no signature seen. (4) Small circular etching of scattered chairs/tables in a faux-brick timber frame, pencil edition lower left (looks like x/10) and pencil signature lower right, illegible, dated '79. (5) Sepia pen and wash of a double-decker tram (Hong Kong style) in a street, signed lower left 'Colin C...' (Crichton? not confirmed).
